newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's ASC probes Bank Melbourne trade.
newsitem.headline: Australia's ASC probes Bank Melbourne trade.

text.p: The Australian Securities Commission (ASC) said on Wednesday that it had launched inquiries into unusual trading of Bank of Melbourne Ltd shares on the eve of last month's bid for the regional bank by Westpac Banking Corp.
"We have had it referred to us by the Australian Stock Exchange," ASC spokeswoman Irene O'Brien told Reuters.
Bank of Melbourne shares rose eight per cent on April 2 before a trading halt was called. The next day, Westpac announced a A$1.435 billion friendly bid for the company.
Westpac managing director Bob Joss has said his bank was not buying Bank of Melbourne shares on April 2.
"The ASX believes there is some reason for concern and we will have a closer look at it and we will decide within a certain period...whether there's something in it," O'Brien said.
Westpac's bid for Bank of Melbourne is still awaiting approval by anti-monopolies watchdog the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC).
